_comment: Single source of truth for the prebuilt environment packages that Daisium /
Daisium_Predict / libOpenCyan CI otherwise compiles inside every build run.
Only genuinely SHAREABLE toolchains belong here: a compiler fork and osxcross
with an Apple SDK, whose contents are decided by upstream commits, not by any
one consumer. Debian sysroot trees deliberately do NOT - each repo's carries a
different package set (Daisium's adds libxml2/libicu/zlib and a cross gcc,
libOpenCyan's a third set), so publishing one repo's tree for another to restore
would freeze someone else's package list here. Those stay produced by each
repo's own prepare_*_sysroot.sh in its own job.
`family` is the contract with the consumers: a CI step asks for one family by
name and gets the newest version this table produces. The name carries everything
that changes the bytes (SDK version, target list, which repo's recipe built it).
prepare/verify run from this repo's workspace with the checkouts named in
`repos` cloned alongside it. dest/markers use shell paths and glob patterns.

release.title: Prebuilt build-environment packages
release.notes: Shared toolchains that the Daisium / Daisium_Predict / libOpenCyan build scripts otherwise compile from source during a build. Consumed by those repos' CI through compile_scripts/tools/envpkg.sh, between actions/cache and the source build. Rebuilt on demand by .github/workflows/envpkgs_compiler.yaml; each asset carries .envpkg.json with the upstream commits, SDK digests and toolchain version it was built from. Debian sysroot trees are intentionally not published here - each repo needs a different package set inside its sysroot.

packages.desc: Hikari OLLVM 23 (clang+lld) built from source with LLVM_TARGETS=X86;LoongArch - the prebuilt clang23 release has no LoongArch backend, so linuxloong64 has to compile it
osxcross target tree (wrappers + cctools-ld64 + Apple SDK 11.3) built with Daisium/Daisium_Predict's recipe: UNATTENDED=1 + MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0, installed into the checkout's own target/
osxcross tool tree built through libOpenCyan's own prepare_osxcross.sh (TARGET_DIR driven, no deployment target pinned); that repo points OSXCROSS_ROOT straight at this dir
